title: UPDATE: Nvidia Backs Franco-German Open AI Research Push in Paris
summary:
Nvidia's chief executive coordinated with President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace to implement the Open Agent Safety Platform and expand computing infrastructure for French enterprises. During the meeting, Jensen Huang pledged support for a joint Franco-German initiative to advance open AI research to maintain regional technological sovereignty. This expansion includes a strategic partnership with Mistral AI, which utilized 4,000 Grace Blackwell chips to train its most recent model.

The initiative follows an announcement that Nvidia will invest $2B in new European AI projects next week, bringing the total committed over the past year to $10B. This funding includes minority stakes in French startups Doctolib, Genesis AI, Pigment, and Entalpic, alongside a planned data center buildout in Europe. Huang is currently on a regional tour with visits to London and Berlin for GTC Berlin, where he has urged Europe to accelerate its AI development to keep pace with the U.S.

selectedTweets.text:
NVIDIA $NVDA PLANS TO ANNOUNCE $2 BILLION IN NEW EUROPEAN INVESTMENTS OVER THE NEXT WEEK

"Europe needs to get in the race."

CEO Jensen Huang said it in Paris on the first day of a tour that also takes him to London and Berlin, per Bloomberg. The new money comes on top of the $8 billion Nvidia has put into Europe over the last year.

He also announced new investments in four French startups:
Doctolib: appointment booking and admin software for doctors
Genesis AI: AI for robots
Pigment: AI-powered business software
Entalpic: AI for chemistry and materials research

Huang also pitched open-source AI models as Europe's way to catch up to the US, saying they "can be customized for languages and for your own sovereignty." Nvidia is a key partner to France's Mistral AI, whose latest model was trained on 4,000 Grace Blackwell chips.
